headline: Sheikh Rabiul Alam says Awami League has been abandoned and banned
summary: The Road Transport and Railways Minister stated that the party became an opponent of the people and was forced to flee the country.
details: Road Transport and Railways Minister Sheikh Rabiul Alam stated that the Awami League has been abandoned and banned because it acted as an opponent to the people.
Speaking at a tree planting program in Sirajdikhan, Munshiganj, on Tuesday, he claimed the party was forced to flee the country and that its activities were banned because the nation desired it.
The Minister added that the legitimacy of a political party is granted by the people and the law.
During the same event, Sheikh Rabiul Alam also discussed plans for renewable energy using government land.
He mentioned that government land under various ministries is being identified and categorized based on size, with solar power projects planned for plots larger than three acres.
The Minister noted that up to one megawatt of electricity can be produced on land exceeding three acres, which will be used locally and supplied to the national grid.

headline_marked: DMP arrests 118 in day-long sweep, including [[26 banned Awami League activists]]
headline: DMP arrests 118 in day-long sweep, including 26 banned Awami League activists
summary: The crackdown took place across various Dhaka Thanas ahead of the Awami League's founding anniversary to prevent potential unrest.
details: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) arrested 118 people during a day-long operation across various Thanas on Monday. Among those detained are 26 members of the Awami League and its associate organizations, whose activities are currently banned.

The operation was conducted as a preemptive measure ahead of the Awami League's founding anniversary on Tuesday. To maintain law and order, the Bangladesh Army and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) were also deployed across the capital and other parts of the country.

Regarding the Awami League arrests, Dhanmondi police held 10 people, Mohammadpur police arrested eight, and Ramna and Khilkhet police arrested two each. One person each was arrested in Bangshal, Kadamtali, Mirpur, and Turag.

In addition to the political arrests, the DMP detained 82 others on various criminal charges. This includes 37 accused drug traders, 33 people linked to robbery, mugging, and piracy, and two extortion suspects.
The Detective Branch (DB) also conducted separate operations, arresting 10 more individuals—six for drug offences and four for fraud, forgery, and theft.
The DMP stated that these operations will continue to ensure public safety and maintain law and order in the city.
caption:
118 people arrested in a single day. DMP cracks down on banned AL activists and criminals to prevent unrest.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) arrested 118 people during a day-long operation across various Thanas on Monday. Among those detained are 26 members of the Awami League and its associate organizations, whose activities are currently banned.

The operation was conducted as a preemptive measure ahead of the Awami League's founding anniversary on Tuesday. To maintain law and order, the Bangladesh Army and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) were also deployed across the capital and other parts of the country.

Regarding the Awami League arrests, Dhanmondi police held 10 people, Mohammadpur police arrested eight, and Ramna and Khilkhet police arrested two each. One person each was arrested in Bangshal, Kadamtali, Mirpur, and Turag.

In addition to the political arrests, the DMP detained 82 others on various criminal charges. This includes 37 accused drug traders, 33 people linked to robbery, mugging, and piracy, and two extortion suspects.

The Detective Branch (DB) also conducted separate operations, arresting 10 more individuals—six for drug offences and four for fraud, forgery, and theft.

The DMP stated that these operations will continue to ensure public safety and maintain law and order in the city.
